entities.summary:
The Battle of Prague was a pivotal event in the Seven Years' War, taking place on May 6, 1757, in the heart of Prague, Bohemia. This decisive battle saw Friedrich II of Prussia face off against the combined forces of the Austrian Empire and the Electorate of Saxony, with the outcome determining the fate of Central Europe. As the Prussian army emerged victorious, the battle marked a turning point in the war, shifting the balance of power in the region.

The consequences of the Battle of Prague were far-reaching. The Prussian victory allowed Friedrich II to expand his territories, gaining control over Silesia and cementing his position as a dominant force in Central Europe. This, in turn, set the stage for the rise of Prussia as a major power, with significant implications for the balance of power in Europe.

The legacy of the Battle of Prague can be seen in the subsequent wars and alliances that shaped the fate of Europe. The Prussian-led coalition of European powers, which included Britain and Russia, would go on to play a crucial role in the Napoleonic Wars, ultimately contributing to the downfall of the French Empire. As the Prussian Empire expanded, its influence extended beyond Central Europe, shaping the course of world history.

In the words of Friedrich II himself, 'The Battle of Prague was a triumph of Prussian arms and a testament to the bravery and discipline of our soldiers.'
